articles.title: Alex Scott: Bournemouth midfielder withdraws from England duty and could miss 'several weeks' with tendon injury
articles.summary: Alex Scott has withdrawn from the England squad due to an injury he picked up during the 7-0 win against Croatia; Scott is set to return to Bournemouth for further assessment; initial scans suggest he could be missing for several weeks; Scott impressed in first start against Croatia
articles.body:
Sky Sports News understands Scott is set to return to Bournemouth for further assessment to discover the full extent of the injury.

Initial indications suggest he could be missing for several weeks, although further scans are planned.

During his pre-Czech Republic press conference, England boss Tuchel revealed more about the injury and how it happened. He said there was no indication that Scott should not play against Croatia.

He explained: "With Alex it's a strange one. I'm very sad about it. He trained in both sessions before the match. He did extra work after the training sessions.

"We knew he was in treatment but we only got green lights from him and the medics. When we were aware of slight discomfort during the match we asked if he wanted to come off. He said no.

"Afterwards he said it was the right decision but he could've played the full 90. He didn't feel an injury. Even on the plane here [to London] before we did the scan. It is a strange one because it does not match the objectivity of the scan and the prediction of the time he is going to miss. There was no awareness of any risk from our side.

"I feel sad for him. We have an exchange all the time and when he went out, even the day after, he didn't feel injured so in my mind, he started tomorrow."

There are media reports that Bournemouth are unhappy that one of their star players has come back from international duty with an injury, and that he should not have played in Rijeka.

"The medical and physical department is in constant contact with all the players who are with us," he said when asked about the club's response. "We are sharing information and this is a totally open process.

"I can totally understand that Bournemouth are not happy and sad because they lose a key player, but I can say from the moment we took the decision to let him play, there was absolutely no risk whatsoever apparent to me or our physical staff that we have risk of an injury.

"I have not taken any risks, even if it was a big opportunity for him and we wanted him to start. If I had the slightest idea there was a risk, I would not have taken it. I would never do this... It's a one-off."

Scott's grandfather died while he was away with England during this international break, but he decided to stay and play in honour of a man he was very close to.

It is understood his grandfather was one of his biggest fans and closest supporters throughout his football career.

Scott impressed on his first England start in Rijeka and drew praise from Tuchel, linking up well with Elliot Anderson , with whom he won the U21 Euros in 2025.

The midfielder asked to come off in the second half after feeling pain.

Sky Sports News reported Arsenal , Manchester City, Manchester United and Chelsea were interested in signing Scott this summer, but Bournemouth remained adamant he was not for sale and were under no pressure to sell, with two years remaining on his contract.

Scott has turned down a new deal at the club amid strong interest from other clubs in the Premier League.

Bournemouth play Chelsea in their first game after the international break at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Konsa returns to Arsenal after leaving England camp

Ezri Konsa has also returned to Arsenal after being ruled out of England's final game of the international break with the Czech Republic on Tuesday.

Konsa has been struggling with a slight muscle injury during the international break which forced him to miss training last week.

He returned to play the full 90 minutes in England's 7-0 win over Croatia on Saturday night but will now play no further part in the Three Lions' lengthy international camp.

He will head to Arsenal for further assessment on his fitness.

Tuchel added on Konsa: "Ezri came into camp with discomfort. Played against Spain which made it worse. He stayed in camp and tried everything for the match in Croatia and gave the green light.

"Unfortunately, he got another hit on the quad and it caused some light trauma. We decided to not let him play again through the pain. Nothing major but not worth taking the risk."

Arsenal return to Premier League action on Saturday as Leeds are the visitors to the Emirates Stadium at 12.30pm.

The key games Scott will miss for Bournemouth

October 10: Chelsea (a) - Premier League

October 15: Sturm Graz (h) - Europa League

October 18: Sunderland (h) - Premier League, live on Sky Sports

October 22: AC Milan (h) - Europa League

articles.title: David Gordo, sobre la recuperación exprés de Fran González: "Había riesgo de lesión y preferimos que no sea con nosotros"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador sub-21 aclara la titularidad del portero sevillista ante el Aston Villa tras dejar la concentración de la selección
articles.summary: El seleccionador sub-21 aclara la titularidad del portero sevillista ante el Aston Villa tras dejar la concentración de la selección
articles.body: Fran González fue el primer internacional del Sevilla que volvió del parón de selecciones. El lunes de la semana pasada, la Real Federación Española comunicó que el guardameta leonés abandonaba la concentración de la selección española sub-21 por unas molestias en el psoas, cediendo su lugar al bético Manu González. A su regreso a la capital hispalense continuó con su proceso de recuperación trabajando al margen de sus compañeros. Sin embargo, sorprendentemente no solo partió como titular en el Trofeo Antonio Puerta, sino que disputó el partido completo. David Gordo, seleccionador español sub-21, respondió acerca de la pronta recuperación de Fran González en una entrevista con Carrusel Deportivo: "Puede ser extremo, pero son casos muy concretos que estudiamos y valoramos. Había riesgo de lesión o de que se pudiera agravar una molestia que tiene y preferimos que eso no sucediera con nosotros. La salud de los jugadores es primordial y nunca queremos que les pase nada, pero si les tiene que pasar, que sea fuera de nuestras concentraciones". "Tenemos siempre tres porteros en la concentración que tienen un nivel extraordinario. Fran tenía molestias y decidimos que cualquiera de los otros podía jugar, como pasó con Bruno, que jugó los 90 minutos contra San Marino a un nivel muy bueno. Estamos muy contentos con los porteros que tenemos", insistió David Gordo, que quiso aportar más argumentos a la decisión. "Tenemos muy poco tiempo para preparar los partidos y necesitamos que todos estén al máximo nivel en cada entrenamiento. Si un jugador, por lo que sea, no lo está, preferimos traer a otro", aclaró. A pesar de las dudas que puedan haber surgido en torno a las molestias de Fran González, David Gordo expresó su satisfacción por verle recuperado y siendo protagonista ante un equipo tan exigente como el Aston Villa: "En el caso de Fran, pues que haya jugado 90 minutos contra un rival de ese nivel le va a ayudar a crecer, a seguir mejorando y a demostrar lo muy buen portero que es". Antes de regresar a Sevilla, el portero del Sevilla formó parte de la selección sub-21 que cayó a domicilio ante Finlandia, aunque tuvo que ver el encuentro desde el banquillo.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal dispute happening against the backdrop of Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell feels fitting
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi awaits his farewell game for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo is embroiled in a bitter dispute with Portugal. Adam Bate looks at two careers entwined once more and wonders whether there is any way for Ronaldo to have his own satisfactory ending...
articles.body:
For Messi enthusiasts, the temptation is to conclude that it tells you everything about the two men. For Ronaldo's more vociferous fans, it is proof of a player not being given his due. Why is he not being afforded such status after doing so much for his country?

Ronaldo started the narrow win over Wales without scoring but was benched for the trip to Norway and was so frustrated by not coming on that he departed the camp. Portugal won that match and coach Jorge Jesus has followed it up with two more in his absence.

"I am not apologising to anyone," said Jesus in the aftermath. "If I need you for 30 minutes, you will play. If I don't need you, you won't play. No player will ever change my ideas as a coach. Not him, not any president, no one." It was not exactly placatory.

"In due course, I will tell the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons behind my departure." That was Ronaldo's own dark declaration, hinting at a justifiable explanation for all this. Jesus has since left the door ajar but is Ronaldo ready to walk through it?

Jesus and Ronaldo worked together at Al Nassr with no indication that it would implode like this. But their characters put them on this collision course. The cantankerous Jesus was never likely to be prone to the obsequiousness that undermined his predecessor.

And so, faced with a Nations League game in which Portugal were holding on for a precious victory away to Erling Haaland's Norway, Jesus was guided by game state not the glorification of the superstar warming up on his bench. It proved an incendiary call.

The precise details of it were hardly predictable. But it is difficult to escape the feeling that on some level this was always coming. This is a 41-year-old man fighting a battle he cannot win. Not against the Portuguese football administration but against time itself.

Ronaldo is two years older than Messi. He is beyond the age at which Pele was filming Escape to Victory and the bloated figure of Diego Maradona was enjoying Boca Juniors wins from his balcony. Johan Cruyff was coaching Barcelona at 41 not playing for them.

But this is not a man capable of accepting competition, of appreciating that Goncalo Ramos, a £60m signing by AC Milan just this summer, might be worthy of minutes instead of him. Every decision risks disrespect, every slight becomes easily magnified.

His admirers will insist that this is part of what has made him great and there is doubtless some truth to it. Scaling such heights in the game is astonishing enough as it is. Without an ego and a certain main-character energy it is surely all but impossible.

As such, the tragedy of this story is that the very trait that caused him to soar is the same quality in him that has brought it all crashing down in the end. How do you persuade Portugal's sporting colossus to be a squad player? It turns out to be tricky.

Ronaldo has dedicated his life to being the very best, not to sitting on the bench and hoping for a cameo. And certainly not to be told that he will be playing 30 minutes away to Norway only to discover that the coach has had a change of heart once in Oslo.

Ronaldo has long faced accusations of selfishness. There were always the understated celebrations on the rare occasions when he was not central to the success. But it rarely reared its head when his own feats was so obviously tied to the fortunes of the team.

The problem was always likely to come when what is best for Ronaldo and what is best for Portugal became misaligned. There had been hints of that under Fernando Santos and certainly under Roberto Martinez. It has fallen on Jesus to manage the inevitable.

Maybe this is not yet the end. Jesus himself has suggested that the situation is easily resolvable. It remains unthinkable that there will not be some sort of send-off akin to the one that Messi will enjoy in the Estadio Monumental in front of 80,000 adoring fans.

There is even a scenario where Ronaldo scores his 1000th goal while wearing a Portugal shirt. But while Messi's big day will be a messianic celebration, expect Ronaldo's finale, whenever it finally comes, to be one fraught with tension, a vast ego being managed.

articles.title: Top 6 Overreactions after Week 5 of 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: The more we play, the more we learn. It's that simple.
articles.body:
The more we play, the more we learn. It's that simple.

As college football says farewell to Week 5 and welcomes Week 6 with open arms, we suddenly find ourselves deep enough into the season to start drawing sizable conclusions.

Then again, doing so is dangerous. One week, Florida is on top of the college football universe; the next, it's getting absolutely manhandled. Such is life in the SEC.

Elsewhere, we saw breakout performances, shocking losses that could result in massive changes and more.

Here are our biggest overreactions from Week 5.

Penn State Has Rapidly Regressed Under Matt Campbell

Penn State's schedule in Matt Campbell's debut season looked delightfully manageable.

Now, after a second-half collapse against Wisconsin and an ugly 21-point loss to Northwestern, one can't help but wonder what the rest of this year—and beyond—will look like in Happy Valley.

Under James Franklin, Penn State largely won the games it should have. That wasn't the issue. The problem was largely his inability to go beyond that ceiling and take the program to new heights.

But now? Penn State finds itself coming off multiple losses to programs it is expected to handle. And the optics of those losses on both sides of the ball were ugly.

Granted, Campbell needs time. His tenure won't be defined by two ugly weekends in the first half of his first season. With that firmly acknowledged, the vibes are not spectacular, and they likely won't be anytime soon.

Keelon Russell Will Be No. 1 Overall Pick in 2028

Thankfully, we still have plenty of time to enjoy Alabama's starting quarterback, who is just getting his feet wet.

But even in the infancy of his college football career, Keelon Russell is doing extraordinary things for the Crimson Tide.

Forget about stats, although we'll get to those. Against Mississippi State, there were plenty of throws that seemingly flipped the game on its side. Russell's arm coupled with his ability to extend plays was on full display yet again.

As for those stats, he has those, too. Through five games, he has scored 15 touchdowns and just two interceptions. He had one really rough half against Kentucky, although he's been nearly perfect otherwise.

The NFL, in many respects, can wait. Alabama plays Georgia next week, and the result of that game will impact this college football season in a major way.

That said, scouts are drooling. Russell, just a true sophomore, is dynamic. And in 2028, he will be the first name called come draft time.

Bryce Underwood Will Be Starting for a New Team Next Fall

It just isn't working. That about sums it up.

For all the physical talent Bryce Underwood possesses, his play has been wildly inconsistent. And with so much change at Michigan, coupled with his early struggles, the future for the former 5-star recruit is clear.

And it doesn't involve his current school.

He needs a change of scenery. The program needs a new starting quarterback. This football marriage isn't working. Period.

In fact, it's hard to know how much longer he'll be the starter. Head coach Kyle Whittingham teased the possibility of making a quarterback change earlier in the year. And while Underwood has still shown flashes, his two-interception performance against Minnesota feels like the beginning of the end.

Given the talent, teams will still line up to recruit him. (Lane Kiffin comes to mind.)

Time will tell what the future holds, although it's increasingly likely it won't be at Michigan.

Speaking of transfer quarterbacks, enter DJ Lagway.

Not terribly long ago, he was a 5-star recruit and one of the most exciting young quarterbacks in college football. At Florida, we saw glimpses of brilliance along with plenty of turnovers.

Lagway transferred to Baylor, and the early returns weren't exactly dazzling. Against Arizona State on Saturday night, however, he was sensational, throwing for 306 yards and accounting for five touchdowns.

An ankle injury sidelined Lagway for multiple weeks, although the QB has been productive when healthy. He has nine touchdowns and only two interceptions in three games.

In terms of size and skills, Lagway has always been intriguing. He's 6'3" and nearly 240 pounds. The football flies out of his hand. It's no wonder he was one of the most coveted quarterbacks coming out of high school, because he often looks the part.

Here's to hoping we see more of what we just witnessed on Saturday.

Jesse Legree is the Biggest Star in CFB You Don't Know (Yet)

Something spectacular is happening in Corvallis.

Jesse Legree, a true freshman wide receiver, is the most dominant player to play the position not named Jeremiah Smith. His five-catch, 156-yard, three-touchdown performance against Colorado State wasn't some random outlier.

In his first five collegiate games, Legree has gone over 100 yards each time. He caught eight passes for 240 yards earlier in the season against Texas Tech. Now, he enters Week 6 with nine receiving touchdowns, which matches what Smith has done at Ohio State.

He wasn't viewed as a can't-miss prospect. If he had been, his recruitment likely would have included more high-profile programs. His 5'10", 175-pound frame may have contributed to that evaluation, as he does not have the size of a prototypical outside receiver.

To date, though, this hasn't slowed him down one bit.

No, we're not talking about where he's playing next year despite the growing questions that emerge each and every time he dominates a football game. Let's save that for another month or two.

Instead, we're going to tune in to celebrate one of the sport's most unlikely stars.

The SEC Will Once Again Cannibalize Itself

The SEC is very good. Through five weeks, it's clear this is the premier conference in all of college football.

With that honor comes some pain. This week, we saw unbeaten Mississippi State and Florida run right into brick walls. These weren't just losses; these were lopsided, potentially resume-crushing defeats.

The gauntlet SEC teams will go through before the end of the season is real. Another undefeated team will fall next week when Alabama plays Georgia in one of the more exciting games of the season.

But the real damage will come to teams looking to finish the season with two losses or less: Alabama, Georgia, Texas, Florida, LSU, Ole Miss, Missouri, Tennessee and others will try to avoid that dreaded third loss that has been a playoff eliminator so far.

Last season, the playoff committee once again took that stand. Will that group react differently this year when the losses start to mount, or will the same formula unfold?

articles.summary: Former Swindon, Hibernian and Crawley striker Harry McKirdy retires from professional football at the age of 29.
articles.body:
Former Swindon Town, Hibernian and Crawley Town striker Harry McKirdy has announced his retirement from professional football, at the age of 29.

McKirdy was released by League Two side Crawley at the end of last season.

Writing on his Instagram account , external , McKirdy said: "After 14 years in full-time football, it's time to call it a day.

"I never thought I'd pack it in so early but sitting here where I am, happy in life, great people around me... how could I possibly have any regrets?"

McKirdy came through the youth ranks at Stoke City and Aston Villa, and made his senior debut at the start of a loan spell with Stevenage in 2016.

He had further loans at Crewe Alexandra and Newport County before being released by Villa in 2019.

McKirdy then played for Carlisle United and Port Vale before joining Swindon Town in August 2021.

He was named in the EFL League Two team of the season and and won Swindon's player of the season award for the 2021–22 campaign after scoring 24 goals in 44 games in all competitions.

Scottish Premiership club Hibernian signed him for an undisclosed fee in September 2022 but he failed to score in 33 games, mostly off the bench, and also had heart surgery during his time north of the border.

He returned to Swindon Town on loan in February 2024 and then had a short spell with Bromley.

McKirdy joined Crawley in June 2025 , scoring eight goals in 33 appearances last season.

articles.title: Women's Super League takeaways: Manchester City and London City dominate
articles.summary: After five frantic weeks, the Women's Super League takes a two-week break, offering the perfect chance to take stock of a thrilling start to the season.
articles.body:
After five frantic weeks, the Women's Super League takes a two-week break, offering the perfect chance to take stock of a thrilling start to the season.

Here are five key takeaways from the opening weeks.

London City back up pre-season ambitions

For the first time this decade, the established order of the WSL looks under threat.

London City Lionesses and Tottenham have been bullish about climbing the table, while Liverpool also sought to kick on this season.

After five games, London City look the most convincing, with Sunday's statement 6-1 win at Spurs a dazzling example of the talent and depth manager Eder Maestre has at his disposal.

Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas headlined some eye-catching summer signings and she scored twice against Tottenham.

But it was the manner in which the whole team dismantled their previously impressive opponents that was so spectacular, with fellow forwards Kadidiatou Diani and Danielle van de Donk also looking a class above.

"This kind of win can be a game-changer," Maestre said.

No doubt. It is the kind of display that can lead to talk of a title charge.

For Spurs, a humiliating home loss is a reality check after promising early results.

Liverpool acquitted themselves well in narrow losses away to both Manchester clubs but, with key attacking players such as Vivien Endemann missing against United, they lacked creativity.

That points to perhaps the biggest thing both Liverpool and Spurs lack in comparison with London City: squad depth.

Five wins from five with 16 goals scored, defending champions Manchester City have picked up where they left off.

Sunday's comeback victory over Arsenal made it City's best start to a season since opening the 2017-18 campaign with seven straight victories, cementing their status as the team to beat.

In so doing, City also likely ended the Gunners' title aspirations even this early on.

It helps when their best players are performing. Khadija Shaw's contract renewal in the summer was key and the striker has five league goals already. England winger Lauren Hemp is also in fine form, contributing four goals and two assists.

After some quietly shrewd additions in Beth Mead, Carlotta Wamser and Niamh Charles, City look well set once again.

Their closest rivals are Chelsea, who have responded to an opening-day draw against Aston Villa by winning four straight games without conceding a goal.

While boss Sonia Bompastor wants them to be more clinical, their defensive strength is something they have over City.

As for Arsenal, the gap is 10 points to leaders City, and strong pre-season hopes of a first league title since 2018-19 are vanishing, with manager Renee Slegers conceding on Sunday: "At the moment, we are not in the conversation."

Manchester United's summer of upheaval bled into the start of the season, with Eva Olid's arrival from Hearts beginning with convincing defeats by London City and Chelsea.

The message from the club was that this would be a season of transition but recent performances suggest they are getting to grips with her style of play.

Saturday's 1-0 win over Liverpool was United's fourth straight victory in all competitions, with 18 goals scored in the process.

"I am so happy for the players - they deserve it," Olid said. "We have started to click in a lot of things and they fight for each other.

"But there is still a lot to improve. We created chances, but our last pass and our finishing needs to be better."

Summer signing Andrea Medina has been a huge positive on the left wing, with her contribution to the team more pronounced than a single goal suggests.

A trip to bottom side Charlton after the break is a presentable chance for more points before a stern test against Manchester City the following weekend.

This season is the WSL's biggest ever, literally, with the league expanding from 12 to 14 teams and three coming up from WSL 2.

Crystal Palace look the most comfortable of the promoted sides, boasting six points from five games and they moved to eighth in the WSL table by drawing at Aston Villa on Sunday.

But things are more difficult for the other promoted sides, Birmingham and Charlton, who prop up the table.

Despite some promising patches, WSL 2 champions Birmingham have just two points and one of those came against Crystal Palace.

At least France forward Oceane Hurtre looks suited to this level, sitting as joint top scorer in the WSL with five goals from five games.

Hurtre scored against Everton in defeat on Sunday but defender Neve Herron summed things up by saying Blues were "second to everything" after the game.

Meanwhile, it looks bleak for Charlton, bottom of the table with zero points, 15 goals against and only two goals scored.

After their 5-1 loss to Brighton on Sunday, goalkeeper and captain Sophie Whitehouse said: "It just wasn't good enough.

"It's a tough league. The jump up is so big. You can't make any mistakes."

Finally, it is too soon to draw conclusions but attendances at some of the league's biggest matches have been down on previous seasons.

For instance, Chelsea hosted Arsenal on 27 September in a fervent atmosphere, but the game had 36% fewer in Stamford Bridge than in January this year.

Similarly, Liverpool against Everton at Anfield was 19% down on last season, albeit the Merseyside derby was the first game of the 2025-26 season.

Three Saturdays ago, Arsenal kicked off against Manchester United at 17:30 in front of 29,853 fans. Last season, it was a lunchtime fixture that welcomed 37,627.

For balance, it ought to be highlighted that the Manchester City v Arsenal game on Sunday was promoted from the Joie Stadium to Etihad Stadium, and definitely had more than the 4,300 who attended the game last season.

Official figures have yet to be released for it.

Nevertheless, while this is a small sample size, paying customers is a potential trend to monitor as the WSL wrestles with the continued challenge of the schedule.

articles.title: Luke Humphries hoping to face Luke Littler in World Championship final after ending major drought at World Grand Prix
articles.summary: Luke Humphries claims first major title since 2025 Premier League with comeback victory over Gerwyn Price; World Grand Prix trophy puts 'Cool Hand' outright fifth on list of all-time PDC major winners; watch Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14
articles.body:
Humphries landed a first major title since the 2025 Premier League as he recovered from 3-0 down to beat Gerwyn Price 6-4 in the final of the double-start event, sealing victory with an 11-darter having broken his opponents in 10 to clinch the ninth set.

'Cool Hand' defeated Littler to win the 2024 World Championship and last year's Premier League but has lost his last four major finals against 'The Nuke', including at the 2025 World Grand Prx.

Humphries, who played four days in a row in Leicester last week, says winning in set-play has given him confidence ahead of the similar format at Alexandra Palace from December 11, live on Sky Sports .

The world No 2 told Sky Sports : "Four days on the trot is hard but I have done it so many times before. I know in the Worlds you have three gruelling days - quarters, semis, final.

"Now I have got that major tournament, it is going to put me in a good frame of mind that I can go on and win the World Championship again.

"My goal now is to make the World final and play [Littler] in it again and let's see what can happen. The real fans of darts know I am still here and capable of winning stuff.

"I have come so close to beating Luke in some majors in the last six to eight months and I think he enjoys the battle as well.

"He deserves credit for what he has done in the sport. He is one of my closest friends on tour. I know a lot of people don't like that but I do because he is such a great kid.

"He is amazing for the sport and the hate he gets is unjust."

'If I am in this game for another 15, 20 years, how much more can I win?

Humphries now has nine PDC major trophies, placing him outright fifth on the all-time list, behind only Phil Taylor, Michael van Gerwen, reigning world champion Littler and James Wade.

"Nine major titles and two World Cups is insane and it's been done in such a short space of time as well - three years to the day," said Humphries, whose maiden major came at the 2023 World Grand Prix when he also beat Price in the final.

"If I am in this game for another 15, 20 years, how much more can I win?

"It's not just one player winning everything. There are so many opportunities now, so many major tournaments. This is great for my confidence and hopefully I can pick up another big one this year.

"I am here and I'm still going to win some stuff. Those last four legs [against Price], I don't think anyone would have stopped me. I felt so focused, so determined.

"After three or four months of not playing your best, people discredit you and think, 'he is finished, he won't win anything' but I always seem to bounce back and pop up with a major tournament or final."

Humphries sported a scab on his head during the World Grand Prix, which he attributed to an allergic reaction to make-up applied during filming for TV show bullseye.

The 31-year-old joked 'Harry Potter did well, didn't he?!' when speaking on stage after beating Price and later added to Sky Sports : "It has been a big story of the week.

"I think I am alright but maybe it got infected or something so I will get that sorted."

The European Tour season continues with the Swiss Darts Trophy (October 9-11) and the Dutch Darts Championship (October 16-18) before the European Championship takes place in Dortmund, Germany from October 22-25.

articles.title: Hjulmand inicia la 'operación retorno' en un Atlético entre el orgullo y la preocupación
articles.standfirst: El danés, tras participar en los cuatro partidos con su selección, regresará con 342 minutos en sus piernas, encarnando la alta carga en las piernas de la mayoría de los internacionales
articles.summary: El danés, tras participar en los cuatro partidos con su selección, regresará con 342 minutos en sus piernas, encarnando la alta carga en las piernas de la mayoría de los internacionales
articles.body: Morten Hjulmand, después de cumplir sus cuatro compromisos con Dinamarca saldados con otras tantas titularidades y 342 minutos sobre el verde (dos victorias y dos derrotas), será el primero en regresar al Cerro (al margen de un Grimaldo que abandonó la concentración de España la semana pasada al sentir unas molestias en el muslo que le apartaron del once en el calentamiento) de los 16 internacionales repartidos por el mundo. Una 'operación retorno' que no finalizará hasta el jueves, a dos días de reencontrarse con LaLiga en Mendizorroza, con la incorporación a los entrenamientos de Musso, el Cuti Romero, Giuliano, Julián Álvarez, Jonathan David y Obed Vargas, que disputan sus últimos partidos en la madrugada del miércoles. Un parón en el que el Atlético ha tenido protagonismo por la alta participación de sus internacionales (sólo Grimaldo y Musso se quedaron a cero), que han llegado a celebrar ocho goles (Pubill, Baena, Mendoza, Hancko, Jonathan David, Julián Alvarez, Cuti Romero y Giuliano), a repartir tres asistencias (dos Baena y una Kang-in Lee) y a sumar dos porterías a cero en tres encuentros en el caso de Oblak. Una incidencia, eso sí, que a falta de un último compromiso más, conlleva una preocupación por la importante carga en las piernas de muchos futbolistas y la falta de tiempo de recuperación antes de retomar LaLiga. Así, aunque Pubill y Kang in sólo disputaron dos de los tres partidos de España y Core del Sur, respectivamente, acumulan 180 minutos con la previsión de que aún se verán incrementados. Del mismo modo que Hancko (171) y Baena (169), presentes en los tres duelos de su selección, alcanzando los 169, o Hancko, tras 171 en tres apariciones también. Por no hablar de un Oblak (270) que lo ha jugado todo. Más 'descanso' han tenido hasta ahora Lookman (137) (además no jugará el último amistoso frente a Rusia), Julián Álvarez (135), Mendoza (135), Obed Vargas (126) Jonathan David (121), Cuti (101), Le Normand (90), Esquivel (90) o un Giuliano al que le han bastado 26 minutos para celebrar un gol. No obstante, salvo un Oblak que tiene visos de acabar siendo el más utilizado, el internacional con más kilómetros en las piernas es precisamente Hjulmand, que al menos también es el primero en unirse a la disciplina de Simeone... aunque paradójicamente para una posición bien cubierta tras hacerse fuertes Barrios, Koke y Cardoso durante el parón.

articles.summary: Sorteados los 56 emparejamientos de la eliminatoria a partido único que se disputarán el 27, 28 y 29 de octubre
articles.body: Ya se conocen los 56 enfrentamientos de la Copa del Rey 2026-27 en su primera ronda. Hoy se ha sorteado la eliminatoria del torneo del K.O. en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas, donde ya han aparecido en los bombos 16 equipos de LaLiga EA Sports para unos partidos que se celebrarán entre el 27, 28 y 29 de octubre. Todos menos Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atlético de Madrid y Real Sociedad, los cuatro que disputarán la Supercopa de España a principios de 2027. Un sorteo con el gran atractivo de los emparejamientos de equipos más modestos, desde Regional hasta Primera, Segunda y Tercera RFEF. Los emparejamientos, a partido único y siempre en el campo del equipo de menor categoría, han agrupado a los clubes por proximidad geográfica y buscando, hasta donde ha sido posible, que los clubes de inferior categoría se enfrenten a los de mayor categoría que hayan superado la eliminatoria anterior. El Navalcarnero y el Manacor se han llevado 'el gordo' del sorteo, quedando emparejado con Betis y Villarreal, dos equipos que están jugando la UEFA Champions League en este curso. También recibirán a otros históricos el ganador del AE Prat vs San Rafael, UE Tavernes y el ganador del Sporting de Hortaleza vs Guimar, que se medirán a Athletic, Valencia y Sevilla, respectivamente. Igualmente, dos bombazos regionales, ya que la Copa recupera el derbi entre Xerez CD y Cádiz más de dieciocho años después. Chapín acogerá una eliminatoria entre el conjunto de Segunda Federación y el equipo de Albert Celades, que no se enfrentan en competición oficial desde 2008. Igualmente el Don Benito - Extremadura será otro duelo por todo lo alto. articles.title: Mbappé responde con ironía a la información de Radio MARCA: “Sí, y también me enfadé con mi tía abuela”
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Real Madrid reaccionó en redes a la versión ofrecida por Tintó, quien aseguró que su actitud en el derbi estuvo relacionada con el enfado por la falta de una campaña del club a favor de su Balón de Oro
articles.summary: El delantero del Real Madrid reaccionó en redes a la versión ofrecida por Tintó, quien aseguró que su actitud en el derbi estuvo relacionada con el enfado por la falta de una campaña del club a favor de su Balón de Oro
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé respondió este lunes con ironía a una información difundida en 'La Tribu', la exitosa tertulia dirigida por Raúl Varela en Radio MARCA, sobre los motivos que habrían estado detrás de su actitud durante el último derbi de Madrid. El delantero francés contestó directamente en redes sociales a una publicación de la radio del deporte que recogía las palabras pronunciadas en antena y negó, en tono sarcástico, esa versión. “😂😂😂... sí, pues sí, y yo también me confundí con mi tía abuela también”, escribió Mbappé. Una respuesta con la que el futbolista se toma de forma divertida la información de Javier Tintó, tertuliano de moda, donde relacionaba su comportamiento sobre el terreno de juego con un supuesto enfado con el Real Madrid y con Zinedine Zidane por el Balón de Oro. La polémica nació a raíz de las declaraciones de Tintó en Radio MARCA. Durante su intervención aseguró que Mbappé habría solicitado al club durante la semana del derbi “un esfuerzo” para impulsar su candidatura al Balón de Oro. “A mí lo que me dicen es que la semana del derbi Mbappé pide al club un esfuerzo y que haga una campaña a favor de su Balón de Oro, que es lo que a él le interesa. El club no cede”, explicó. Tintó relacionó directamente esa negativa con la imagen mostrada posteriormente por el delantero en el partido: “Ya me cuadra la actitud de Mbappé en el campo ese derbi porque fue una cosa increíble. No es normal que te quedes con diez y vayas andando por el campo. Estaba con nueve el Madrid y sé que es por eso, es un enfado que tuvo”. Según la misma versión, Mbappé también habría pedido a Zinedine Zidane que apoyara públicamente su candidatura. “Al parecer a Zidane también le pide ese esfuerzo”, añadió Tintó durante su intervención. La contestación del francés no tardó en llegar. Mbappé eligió el sarcasmo para comentar públicamente el relato y convirtió en cuestión de minutos la información de Radio MARCA en uno de los asuntos más comentados alrededor del delantero madridista.

articles.title: 🤝 ADL backs Allegri, Premier League eyes Pio, Lazio news: today’s news 🔥
articles.summary: Tonight, the Italian national team takes to the pitch for its fourth Nations League fixture, the last match before the focus shifts back to clubs and their l...
articles.body:
Tonight, the Italian national team takes to the pitch for its fourth Nations League fixture, the last match before the focus shifts back to clubs and their league and cup commitments.

Meanwhile, let's take a look at today's biggest news.

Juventus are continuing to explore potential reinforcements on the left flank, with Miguel Gutierrez, currently at Bayer Leverkusen, reportedly among the players being monitored. The Spaniard is said to have impressed the club's management with his personality, tactical versatility and attacking qualities.

As Fussball-news.de points out, Carnevali has reportedly placed Gutierrez among his preferred options for the position, but the deal looks particularly difficult financially. Leverkusen consider him an important player and have reportedly set an asking price of between €50 million and €60 million, a figure currently holding Juventus back.

Milan: Estupinan sidelined on international duty

Milan have an issue to contend with during the international break. Pervis Estupinan, away with Ecuador, has experienced discomfort in his left knee that will force him to leave his national team's camp early.

As head coach Gallardo explained, it is a mild knee sprain, and there currently appears to be no particular cause for concern. Estupinan will nevertheless return to Milanello, where Milan's medical staff will assess his condition.

Inter: Premier League clubs target Pio Esposito!

Francesco Pio Esposito continues to earn a bigger role in the plans of Inter and the Italian national team, while attracting a growing number of admirers outside Italy too. The young Inter striker has reportedly caught the eye of several leading Premier League clubs in particular.

According to Calciomercato.com , Arsenal and Manchester United are leading the chase, with the Gunners particularly interested in the forward born in 2005. Should Gyökeres leave, Arsenal have reportedly identified Esposito as one of the ideal candidates to replace him. It is worth noting, however, that the Inter player recently renewed his contract .

Napoli: ADL at Castel Volturno to back Allegri

Aurelio De Laurentiis visited Castel Volturno as Napoli resumed training. The president met with Massimiliano Allegri and Giovanni Manna to take stock of the team's situation and the coming weeks following a below-par start to the season.

According to Sky Sport , the meeting also served to reaffirm the club's faith in Allegri, who remains central to Napoli's project. Meanwhile, Napoli are awaiting the return of several injured players, while McTominay is due to undergo medical assessments to obtain clearance to play following heart surgery.

Roma: Soulé's workload to be managed ahead of Como

Roma are preparing for their clash with Como, and Gasperini will need to carefully assess Matias Soulé's condition. The Argentine, a key performer at the start of the season after a summer dominated by transfer rumours, has repaid his coach's faith and also earned his debut for Argentina.

According to TMW , his late return to Trigoria could prompt Gasperini to manage Soulé's workload ahead of the next league fixture. With Dybala and Molina also returning early, the attacking midfielder could be rested from the start against Como.

Lazio eye Parra but face European competition

Lazio are also looking at the South American market and have reportedly added Neider Parra, Atletico Nacional's Colombian centre-back, to their watchlist. The young defender has attracted interest from numerous European clubs, including Brighton, Bournemouth, Bologna, Nice, Genk and PSV, as well as Ajax and Porto.

According to Il Corriere dello Sport , Parra could represent an attractive opportunity thanks in part to his transfer fee, currently estimated at around €800,000, although a bidding war could drive that figure up. In Colombia, he has drawn comparisons with Davinson Sanchez, while Lazio are waiting to find out whether they will be able to make signings in January.

Fiorentina: dramatic revelation over Nije deal

Alieu Njie joined Fiorentina after a fierce transfer battle. Crystal Palace had tried to muscle in on the deal and reportedly made one final push in the hours immediately before his medical to persuade the Swedish winger to change his destination.

As Njie himself told Expressen , the player born in 2005 was initially attracted by the prospect of moving to the Premier League, but Fiorentina's offer changed his plans. By the time Crystal Palace made another approach, he had already chosen Florence, where he was reunited with Vanoli, the coach who had handed him his Serie A debut at Torino.

articles.title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers reveals saddest part of Joey Porter Jr. trade
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers revealed the most heartbreaking part of the Joey Porter Jr. trade.
articles.body:
Just when it seemed like Joey Porter Jr. was finally set to return to the Pittsburgh Steelers , everything changed in a matter of days. That sad fact isn't lost on Aaron Rodgers, who shared his honest take on the unfortunate trade situation that played out less than 24 hours before the Steelers faced the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football.

Speaking with reporters following the Steelers' Week 4 loss to the Browns, Rodgers revealed what some could argue is the most heartbreaking aspect of this entire trade situation: he thought Porter was actually going to play for the Steelers this week.

"You know, I thought Joey might play this week based on his practice stuff," Rodgers said. "But, you know, we wish Joey well."

That's honestly why the Porter trade felt so surreal. Porter denied previously requesting a trade. He was listed as a full participant in practice on Week 4's injury report on Tuesday and Wednesday, albeit for practice walkthroughs. It felt as though Porter would eventually have to suit up for Pittsburgh, which is why Rodgers and many other fans believed Week 4 was the game it would happen.

Yes, Porter is old news now. It's probably best to push forward and focus on the Steelers who actually love Pittsburgh football. But it does sting being reminded by Rodgers of what could've been in Week 4 or the remainder of the 2026 season.

articles.title: Man City charges: Premier League clubs do not expect City to be in Premier League next season if appeal fails
articles.summary: Man City have lodged their appeal against an independent commission finding them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules; if it fails, City's rivals believe that a points deduction is not sufficient if they return to the top-flight after one year
articles.body:
As City's legal team prepare for their appeal and sanctions hearing after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's rules, their rivals in England and across Europe believe "the punishment should fit the crime".

With the looming prospect of City taking their bid to clear their name all the way to the High Court, rival clubs are becomingly increasingly concerned about the damage that is being done to the image and integrity of the Premier League, the cost of the dispute and what they see as City's failure to take any responsibility or accountability for their actions.

City are adamant they have done nothing wrong, insisting they are innocent and that a "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists" to support their position as they lodged their appeal .

But even a cursory reading of the decision which was published by the independent disciplinary commission puts into sharp focus the scale of the task facing City's lawyers when an appeal hearing takes place before Christmas.

The commission's finding are about as serious as it gets when it comes to financial rule-breaking and the fact that it was carried out over nine seasons and distorted the competition means City's rivals are not expecting Enzo Maresca's team to be playing in the Premier League next season.

Many believe that a points deduction is not a sufficient punishment if it would lead to City spending just one season outside the top flight.

It is only natural for clubs to think of their own self-interest and City's relegation would mean one fewer club going down this season as well as removing one of the favourites from the title race and opening up another European place. Self-interest is not the over-riding consideration though.

The consensus appears to be that rules have to be respected by all clubs, no matter their size or status - and it would not be sufficient to hand City a punishment that would last only one season for rules which were broken across multiple seasons.

City's rival Premier League clubs will not be involved in the sanction hearing, which could be take place while the appeal process runs its course.

The same three-person panel which heard the evidence at the 42-day hearing in 2024 and delivered its core decision last Tuesday will decide on sanctions after the Premier League, as the prosecutors, put forward their recommendation and City's lawyers argue their case.

It will be down to the Premier League board to decide what recommended sanction their lawyers should present to the panel.

In 2023, the Premier League argued that Everton deserved a 12-point deduction for one breach of the Profitability and Sustainability Rules.

Everton, who were in a desperate financial position at the time, eventually ended up with a six-point deduction after they appealed the original 10-point sanction.

With both sides allowed to appeal the sanctions, and City appealing the judgment, Premier League clubs are prepared for this marathon dispute to keep on running until at least next year.

Clubs have been trying to draw a line under the legal disputes which have become a feature of the English game as they try to move towards what some executives call "the NFL model" where the league speaks with one voice.

That will not happen until the final chapter of the 115 charges case is finally written.

articles.title: Arsenal must be accountable for their own failings in faltering Women's Super League season
articles.summary: Digital journalist Laura Hunter returns for a second season with a WSL-dedicated column, analysing all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; this week's focus is on Arsenal's self-doubt and how far they have fallen behind others in the title race after defeat to Man City
articles.body:
Slegers 'fine margins' defence failing to stand up

Renee Slegers has had to put a brave face on things over the past couple of weeks. Arsenal are winless in each of their last four league outings, their worst start to a campaign since 2014. To judge their alarming league position paints a bleaker picture still.

There are not many defensible aspects of such underperformance, despite Slegers' consistent claim that her side are falling foul of fine margins. That argument becomes less and less credible the longer such a stagnant run continues.

Perhaps it even lost its legitimacy completely when Slegers admitted after defeat to Man City that the club will use the upcoming international break to stage a comprehensive review of "not only what we see on matchday, but everything in the background". She added: "We have to turn over every stone."

Small margins do not tend to require such investigation. To suggest Arsenal have been hard done by up until now surely misses the point. Tweaks are not enough to arrest such a talented team from its current malaise. If they were, plenty of stones could be saved from the scour that Slegers has promised over these next two weeks.

In reality, Arsenal appear to be suffering a crisis of confidence, a self-doubt that is particularly noticeable in the pressure moments of big games. It's a multi-pronged problem with tough consequences.

Lisa Baum offered exhibit A within three minutes of kick-off at the Etihad on Sunday, escaping the advances of Niamh Charles, as she did many times throughout the game, only to snatch at a near-post effort instead of squaring the ball to Alessia Russo for a tap-in.

In isolation, that poor decision is easy to write off. Baum is new to the league; a young, dynamic winger with a hunger to impress. Having created the chance, she had every right to take the shot on herself. But choosing the low-probability option seems to be a trend that is harming Arsenal in the final third.

It happened again when Georgia Stanway played a superb raking pass out to Emily Fox on the right and she tried to beat Ayaka Yamashita from an impossible angle. Had she delayed by a fraction of a second, Russo was making a clever run on the blindside of Jade Rose and would have been free at the back post.

Stanway's off-target strike from 30 yards shortly after bore all the same hallmarks, and so a problem becomes a pattern, and that cycle of uncertainty is ruining Arsenal's chances of winning games.

Simply, Arsenal have lost any semblance of nuance. The numbers back that up. Their xG differential is the worst in the division, their conversion rate just as damning. Shots are being snatched at as desperation sets in, doubt stalking the patterns of play by which Arsenal are so known.

This was not a defeat by margins. Man City have killers in their ranks. Arsenal do not. The current conditioning of each side, broken down, is actually quite stark. Nothing about the way City operate under Andree Jeglertz is inhibited. They play with a full range of motion and balanced flow through the thirds when they progress the ball. Each phase has purpose.

Jeglertz lept to the aid of Slegers after the game, calling Arsenal a "great football team" but also made a point to praise his own side's "very fluent" attacking play, adding "we score in different ways".

The creative paralysis Arsenal are suffering does not allow for that, scoring twice because of faults attributed to City's defending. Albeit Russo did offer a timely reminder of her finishing quality in the second half. Her first goal of the domestic campaign is perhaps something to build on; she is one of many with form issues greater than any off-day can accept responsibility for.

Slegers and her coaching staff have serious work to do; by far the toughest examination of her Arsenal tenure so far lies in the next block of fixtures. The north London derby is later this month.

The Dutchwoman has cultivated a discernibly strong bond with her squad and, importantly, retains the backing of the club despite being unable to deliver consistency of results in this moment. Arsenal's stance is not expected to change over the course of this international window.

The time for a reality check is now, though. No more talk of fine margins. Arsenal need big impact from this break and a more intentional way of accepting responsibility for what has already gone wrong in order to find their way back.

The gap to leaders Man City is anything but small or fine. It's a whopping 10 points.
